summary: APM feed s084_single is degraded: 30.4% of TCP sessions (31/102) are one-way, exceeding 10% threshold. APM requires both directions for request/response correlation. All other checks (duplicates, drops, VLANs, encryption, overload) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker/TAP is delivering only one direction of traffic to the tool. Feed name 's084_single' suggests a single capture point or SPAN without aggregation, or asymmetric routing where return path is on a different link not aggregated to this tool port. 31 of 102 sessions show only client->server or server->client.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM needs both directions to measure transaction latency, response time, and TCP handshake/termination. With 30% one-way, APM cannot correlate requests with responses, will miscalculate or miss application performance metrics, produce incomplete flows and false gaps.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregating both forward and reverse directions of each flow to the same APM tool port ensures complete TCP sessions for accurate latency and transaction reconstruction.
